I am not naive enough to expect a linear path forward, especially given recent history, but the year's developments have given me renewed reasons to continue holding the company and allow the story to continue to play out. I am up around 32% on my position as of writing.

$BFIT, after a significant period of being dead money for me, finally seems to be gaining some traction. The company this year announced the acquisition of a German franchise chain and Covid era club openings appear to be improving economics more in line with legacy gyms

It may take time but my personal view is that shares at current prices present a very attractive risk reward profile for new investors and the company is also a victim of negativity around microcap UK stocks. It's trading at 6-7x trough earnings, 3x EV/EBITDA.

On $CHH.L - I will be stubborn on this one, possibly to my detriment. The company's poor trading post Covid has been blamed on a weak hospitality industry and increasing energy prices. Before making a final judgment on this, I need to see one, or both of these headwinds subside.

Despite this, I am more pleased with my ability to identify and buy into an exceptional opportunity. I did my work on Nordrest largely in a bubble before later learning of it's favour amongst some bigger fish. I hope to hold it for a long time and may yet add on a bad Q results.

12) The RSG Spain deal resulted in a doubling of gym EBITDA and they are getting their guided 30%+ returns per club. Stressed this is not a fair comp and they won't get 30% but they still feel it is a good deal for them.

11) During visitations they saw potential for a much higher number of members per club. They feel the issue has been a lack of marketing and feel they can significantly increase this number, especially as the gym locations are good and ones they themselves would have picked.

10) Royalty Fee for CleverFit is lower than comps. There are 60 gyms already due to open in the next year. CFIT had lower club openings in recent years are a result of Covid overhang, similar issues to BFIT.

9) CleverFit have not historically had a big marketing budget and any campaigns would be done locally. BFIT do national ad campaigns. Brand recognition and member base has therefore been pretty low. BFIT are very pleased with the location of around 90% of the gyms.

8) CleverFit can operate smaller gyms that BFIT can. Around 10% of their gyms are run, basically to enable a franchisee to make a salary, perhaps with them doing PT work too. They think they can increase membership by 20% at these small clubs with basic marketing.

7) Management are lowering club opening targets in order to focus on FCF and ensure the franchise integration is successful. This lowering of guidance is solely down to these factors, not any operational changes. I would imagine this is mostly why the stock dipped.

6) 90% of CleverFit gyms share a very similar footprint to BFIT gyms. General rebranding should not be expensive but full rebrand would be more costly as this would include adding full aircon to all clubs (some CFITs don't have this) and €65k per club for staffless camera system

5) The team made contact with CFIT about a potential acquisition in 2019 but it was not for sale. Have got on well with the existing owner. Do not expect any surprising additional transaction costs related to the acquisition.

4) There is a healthy backlog of franchise interest, waitlist of 150+. Was mentioned on the call that CFIT have reduced their gym count in recent years. Despite this, there is clearly interest from potential/existing franchisees to open more, evidence by €4k waitlist costs.

3) CleverFit operational management will stay in place. Owner of the chain will remain involved but take a back seat. I assumed this would be the case as they add franchise expertise and can support in the roll out into new areas and countries. CFIT is a 'well oiled machine.'

2) CFIT have around 165 individual franchisees they now need to engage in conversation about rebranding and adopting the rest of the groups tech. Contracts are standard franchise deals where they are responsible for upgrade costs. Remains to be seen if all clubs will rebrand.

1) They see this acquisition as a way to drive dual growth between both owned clubs and franchised clubs. They have hundreds of targeted locations in France and Spain and this may enable them to grow into these locations faster. Made reference to $mcd and $sbux dual strategy.
